title: The ratzon kadum in circles and in straightness: a will for Himself that holds every detail
overview:
Chapter 17 opens the details of the *Kav*, in circles and in *yosher*, by explaining the *ratzon kadum*. It is the simple will already decided in the Essence, come up in a thought. Its letters are a copy, no longer the Essence's own, yet its content is the same, and it is still a will for Himself: for His own sitting, not for the chair. Knowing Himself, He knows every detail, the way someone who knows a man knows his house. So every creature, a bug, a squirrel, a drunk in the street, is a detail of the King and deserves respect, and the finished house, the end of the seventh millennium, came up first.

The *Zohar* calls it *Atika d'Atikin* and *Atika Stima'a*; it is revealed in the *metzach* of *Atika Kadisha*, *Atik* and *Arich* of *Atzilus*. In the circles each lower level is only the will looking for a reason and proving it right, like a bribe. When the will is put into practice, the order turns over into *yosher*, with the deed outside. Of the *Ein Sof* itself nothing may be said; speech begins with *Adam Kadmon*.

sections.title: The Kav in circles and in straightness: the question the chapter opens
sections.summary: The chapter turns to the details of the *Kav*: it comes as an inner light, becomes a circle, and so on. The *Etz Chaim* says that in the circles the highest is the finest, and in *yosher* (straightness) the opposite.

sections.title: The ratzon kadum: the simple will come up in a thought, still for Himself
sections.summary: The *ratzon kadum* is the same simple will that was already decided in the Essence, once it comes up in a thought. Its letters are a copy, no longer the letters of the Essence, yet its content is exactly the same; and it is still a will for His own enjoyment, not for the thing.

phrases.he: וביאור הדברים, הנה ידוע שבחינת רצון קדום זה,
הגם שלגבי בחינת רצון הפשוט המוחלט בעצמות נקרא התפשטות רצון,
phrases.en: compared to the *Atzmus*, it's called *hispashtus ratzon*

phrases.he: אבל עדיין הוא בהעלם ולא בגלוי כלל
כי אינו רק השפעת והמשכת רצון הפשוט של חפץ חסד שהוחלט בעצמות מכבר, כך יהיה בפועל ממש
phrases.en: it is just simply the same *ratzon pashut* that was already decided, that that's the way it should be

phrases.he: ומיד שעולה במחשבה זאת שיהיה הכל,
phrases.en: and when it came up in an actual *machshava*

phrases.he: הוא הנקרא מחשבה ורצון קדום
phrases.en: that's what's called a *ratzon kadum*

phrases.he: שכולל כל מה שבתוכו רצונות פרטים
כנזכר לעיל במשל הבנין

blocks.text: The same simple will, already decided that this is how it should be; come up in an actual *machshava* (thought), it is the *ratzon kadum* (primordial will), including all the particular wills.
A *machshava* is a separate thing, in letters, as writing is separate from the *sechel* (intellect); only a *machshava* comes up inside of himself.

blocks.question: Was the glif glifu (the engraving of letters before the tzimtzum) not also like that?
blocks.text: No. The *glif glifu* is not really a separate *machshava*; it is still part of the *sechel* itself, not an actual thought.

blocks.question: And what about the reshimu?
blocks.text: The *reshimu* (impression) is the *glif glifu* with the light of the *Atzmus* gone out; but it is still as it was inside Himself, so it still counts as the *Atzmus*.

From the *reshimu* a line of *hispashtus* (spreading) went to the *ratzon kadum*. The *reshimu*'s letters were *mamash* the *glif glifu*'s, without the light; the *machshava kduma*'s are a copy, hence *Atik*. Still it is the *Atzmus*'s thought, on its way out.
Compared to the *Atzmus* it is *mamash* other: the light is gone and the letters are a copy. Yet its content is exactly the same; nothing changed.
So this thought is called a spreading of will compared to the *Atzmus*, yet it is still for His own enjoyment, not for the thing: not the chair, but his own sitting.

phrases.he: אם כן עדיין רצון קדום זה הכל בעצמו
phrases.en: It's really still all inside of Himself

phrases.he: בלתי התגלות לחוץ,
phrases.en: without coming to the outside, without being really revealed to the outside.

blocks.text: So the *ratzon kadum* is really still all inside of Himself, without being revealed to the outside.

sections.title: Everything is made from it: knowing Himself, He knows every detail, down to the end
sections.summary: From the *ratzon kadum*, which is really Himself, everything is made afterwards, as from knowing a man you know his house. Every detail, down to a bug or a drunk in the street, is a detail of the King and deserves respect; and the end of the deed, the finished house, came up first of all.

phrases.he: אבל ממנו נעשה הכל אחר כך

blocks.text: But from it everything is made afterwards: by knowing Himself He knows everything. How, one may ask, if the details were there but not yet as they would be made?

blocks.title: The size of his pants
blocks.text: They are there: know a man, and you know his pants size, because you have his measure. So here He is still not said to know anything outside Himself.

blocks.title: A house for a bird
blocks.text: In the building there is no will yet for a swimming pool, only for swimming; for eating, not a kitchen; for sleeping, not a bedroom. Know him and you know his bedroom: a bird's has a stick in it, and his house has no stairs; you come in from the top. What He knows is not the house but Himself.
Everything is made afterwards from the way He is. The text says "from this *ratzon kadum*", but in it, it is really Himself.

phrases.he: וזהו כי הוא אמר, במחשבה הקדומה,
phrases.en: He said in *machshava kduma*,

phrases.he: ויהי כו'
phrases.en: and then it was.

blocks.text: He said it in the *machshava kduma*, **and then it was**: as far as the *Aibershter* (G-d) is concerned, that finished it, and it came out by itself.

phrases.he: ונקרא חיי כל העולמים
מראש דאדם קדמון עד עקב אדם קדמון בסוף עשיה,
והיינו כל היצור לא נכחד כו'
phrases.en: that nothing is missing

phrases.he: שאין פרט היותר אחרון שלא קדם להיות ברצון ובמחשבה זו
phrases.en: There's nothing that wasn't originally over there.

blocks.text: "No creature is hidden": **that nothing is missing**. Every detail of the final thing has to come with a detail of the *Atzmus* it is prepared for.

blocks.title: The king does not buy off the rack
blocks.text: For a king everything is custom. We buy a suit off the rack, the tailor stretches it, and the color still isn't *mamash* right. We too, as will be said later, have exactly what we want, only we can't necessarily afford it; a king gets wine exactly as he wants, even at a thousand dollars a bottle, and clothes the same. So every detail goes by one in the *machshava kduma*, which goes by Himself; not one thing is left out.
So the creature matters: even a bug is an enclothement of some detail upstairs. "No creature is hidden from You": none can fail to fit something upstairs.

blocks.question: What about the yucky things?
blocks.text: Even the yucky things are still yucky according to something upstairs.

blocks.title: The Atari game in the king's house
blocks.text: Even Amalek, made to be killed? The man's Atari game fights him, and that fits his character: nobody wants an Atari game that says, "Hi, how you doing?" It fits the *midda* of *netzach* (victory).
So nothing in the world is just an enclothement of it: it is *mamash* the *machshava kduma*, *mamash* the *Aibershter*'s stamp, which means His name.

So respect everything: "If you see a squirrel, you're seeing G-d." Whatever He wanted fits some part of Him, as every part of the king's clothing fits the king: spit on his shoe and you spit on the king. Looking at anything, you are literally looking at the *Aibershter*.

No detail, even the very last, was not first in this will and thought: **There's nothing that wasn't originally over there.** So it doesn't matter. You see "some stupid dirty bum walking down the street half drunk" and say, "What about him?" Even the very last detail could not be there unless it was first over there.

phrases.he: ואדרבה
phrases.en: Just the opposite.

phrases.he: סוף מעשה, כמו בסוף אלף הז',
עלה במחשבה קדומה זו תחלה
phrases.en: It came up in this *machshava kduma*

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות

blocks.text: Not that the worlds of *Atzilus* are more *davka* there than we. **Just the opposite.** The end of the deed came up first, as with clothing.

blocks.title: The outermost clothes
blocks.text: It is *davka* the outermost clothes that represent the king: you can't go into the street in your underwear; the honor is in what is on the outside.

blocks.title: The wallpaper, not the studs
blocks.text: So with a house: cement, studs, wires and pipes hold it up, but what you *davka* wanted is the wallpaper. Planning with his wife, "they didn't talk about the studs, they talked about wallpaper," carpet or parquet; the ceiling was the paint, not the drywall.

blocks.title: The chandelier and the decorators
blocks.text: He wanted to please his wife, and what she thought about was the chandelier on the ceiling: the most external level, done at the very end. First the studs, then the drywall, and for the construction crew it is a finished building. Walk in with the wife: "Look at this place, dust all over, and it's not even a floor yet, just plywood!" Now come the decorators. In the first thought, that is how you saw it, not the stuff behind it.

sensitivity.reason: Built on a stock picture of the wife who cares about the chandelier and is unimpressed by the bare building.

blocks.text: So the real thing is *davka* the finished whole of the end of the seventh millennium: the physical world after we have studied *Shaar HaYichud*, with commentaries like *Ayin Beis*, through the thousand years of *Moshiach*; then come the fifty thousand jubilees. **It came up in this *machshava kduma*** first.

sections.title: The Zohar's names: Atika d'Atikin, Atika Stima'a and Atika Kadisha
sections.summary: The *ratzon kadum* is *Atika d'Atikin*, the delight of all delights and the will of all wills, and *Atika Stima'a*, *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*: still hidden, still for Himself. It is revealed in the *metzach* (forehead) of *Atika Kadisha*, *Atik* and *Arich* of *Atzilus*, where the will and delight for each world, and for each detail, come out.

phrases.he: (ובלשון הזהר נקרא עתיקא דעתיקין או עתיקא סתימאה
phrases.en: this *machshava kduma* is called *Atika d'Atikin* or *Atika Stima'a*

phrases.he: והוא בחינת רעוא דכל רעווין עילאין
phrases.en: it's also called the *ratzon* of all the *ratzonos*

phrases.he: דאתגליין במצחא דעתיקא קדישא כו'
phrases.en: these things are revealed in the *metzach* of *Atika Kadisha*

phrases.he: כי ברצון מלובש התענוג,
והיו לאחדים ממש
phrases.en: it's *mamash* one thing

blocks.text: In the *Zohar*'s language **this *machshava kduma* is called *Atika d'Atikin* or *Atika Stima'a***: the hidden *taanug* (delight) of all delights, a delight not in the chair but in sitting.

**It's also called the *ratzon* of all the *ratzonos***, revealed in the *metzach* (forehead) of *Atika Kadisha*, because the delight is dressed in the will and they become one: **it's *mamash* one thing**.

phrases.he: וברצון הפשוט ההיולי
שבחפץ חסד ההיולי (הנזכר לעיל באות יוד ואות יא)
היה כלול בו התענוג הפשוט שבעצמות
שנקרא שעשועי המלך בעצמותו כו'
וגם בג' מדריגות עד שבא בדבר פרט,
אנא אמלוך,
שזה בחינת מלכות דאין סוף שלפני הצמצום
כמו שכתוב שם
הכל בחינת שעשועי המלך בעצמו בטהירו עילאה

blocks.text: The simple delight, *sha'ashuei hamelech* (the King's delight in Himself), is *mamash* above *Atika d'Atikin*, which is already actual delight; there it was the *Atzmus*, *hayah k'lo hayah*. Through *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon*, to *Ana Emloch* before the *tzimtzum*, all is His delight in Himself.

phrases.he: אך עתיקא דעתיקין מקור כל התענוגים
או רעוא דכל רעויין כו',
היינו בבחינת הקו שאחר הצמצום
שכולל כמה רצונות ותענוגים שעתידים לבוא בגלוי

blocks.text: *Atika d'Atikin* is His will for Himself in relation to the *Atzmus*: a preceding will, not for a house but for a home, a will for oneself already related to a house.
Unlike the *ratzon hapashut*, which is Himself, this is a will for Himself, including many wills and delights to come into revelation.

phrases.he: ועתיקא סתימאה הוא בבחינת כתר דאדם קדמון
שהוא בהעלם הרצון והתענוג לעצמו עדיין,
phrases.en: It's really still for Himself

phrases.he: רק שחושב להיות הדבר כך בפועל הגילוי
כמו להיות גילוי הרצון והתענוג להאציל עשר ספירות כו'
(ולכך נקרא עתיקא סתימאה בחינת העלם לגלוי על כל פנים
phrases.en: it's called *Atika Stima'a*: it's already an *Atik*, but it's *stum*

phrases.he: מה שאין כן ראשית הקו נקרא סתימא דכל סתימין
phrases.en: But the *reishis hakav* is called *stima d'chol stimin*,

phrases.he: דגם מחשבה דאדם קדמון לא תפיס ביה כו')
phrases.en: that even *Atika Stima'a* cannot grasp it

phrases.he: ולהיות הרצון והתענוג לברוא כו'

blocks.text: **It's really still for Himself**, but thinking toward revelation: Himself thinking of sitting, so there will be a chair, though He thinks of no chair.

The will and delight to emanate ten *sefiros* is not yet the will for *Atzilus*. **It's called *Atika Stima'a*: it's already an *Atik*, but it's *stum*** (closed). **But the *reishis hakav* is called *stima d'chol stimin*, that even *Atika Stima'a* cannot grasp it**.

phrases.he: ועתיקא קדישא הוא התענוג שבחכמה
והוא בחינת עתיק יומין ואריך אנפין דאצילות,
phrases.en: of *Atzilus*: what is usually called *Atik* and *Arich*

phrases.he: שהרצון והתענוג בא בגלוי
phrases.en: *Atik* and *Arich* is the *taanug* and *ratzon hagalui*; that's where the *gilui* is

phrases.he: כמו שיתבאר הכל דרך פרט)

blocks.question: What was said before, the will of all the upper wills revealed in the forehead of Atika Kadisha, seems to be a higher level than Atik and Arich of Atzilus?
blocks.text: No. *Atika Kadisha* is **what is usually called *Atik* and *Arich***: ***Atik* and *Arich* is the *taanug* and *ratzon hagalui*; that's where the *gilui* is**. There *Raava d'chol Raavin*, the hidden *machshava kduma*, is revealed.

Even *Adam Kadmon* is the hidden will, with no revelation of what it is; that is only in *Atik*. Some places call *Arich* *Atika Kadisha*; here he explains it better: *Atika Kadisha* is the whole *Keser*.

Its main detail is the *metzach*, the part of the *gulgoles* (skull) before the frontal lobe: the will comes into the hidden brain and shows on the forehead, which, various places say, lights up or gets sad.

blocks.title: Seeing through the hat
blocks.text: The big kabbalists can read your forehead. A man told that the *Rebbe* could see his thoughts on his forehead came with his hat pulled down. The *Rebbe* told him: "You think if I can see through your forehead, I can't see through your hat?"
blocks.outOfPlace: The next class (the second side of the tape) goes on with *Atika Kadisha* and its *metzach* before it rereads lines 21-23; kept here, in class order, under the passage being discussed.

blocks.text: *Atik* in *Arich* is the revealed will and delight: to emanate, to create, then *Yetzira* and *Asiya*. The will for *Atzilus*, as said last time, is figuring out in his own head what he wants. So this is *Atika Stima'a*, and *Atika Kadisha* the revealed *Atik*: *Atzilus*, planning the house in his head; *Beriya*, the architect; *Yetzira*, the draftsman; *Asiya*, the contractor.
blocks.outOfPlace: The next class (the second side of the tape) goes on with *Atika Kadisha* and its *metzach* before it rereads lines 21-23; kept here, in class order, under the passage being discussed.

blocks.text: No detail is missing. The intermediary levels, mere conduits, have their own will and delight: planning the house with his wife is such a pleasure that a person can plan and never do anything. "This is called daydreaming."
blocks.outOfPlace: The next class (the second side of the tape) goes on with *Atika Kadisha* and its *metzach* before it rereads lines 21-23; kept here, in class order, under the passage being discussed.

blocks.title: The rabbi and his gvir watch the yeshiva go up
blocks.text: While a new *yeshiva* building went up, the rabbi would come with his big *gvir* (wealthy backer) and stand watching, plainly enjoying it, though others did the building. The building stage itself has its own delight and will.

blocks.title: The artist's picture at the banquet
blocks.text: Before that, at the first banquet, there was only the architect's artist's picture of the building: no building, not even a blueprint, just the concept. And there was a big delight even in that.

blocks.text: There is a big delight even in shopping for a car, and especially in women one sees it: a big delight in the shopping itself, and before that in sitting around talking about what they plan to buy, above all when she is planning her house. There is a big delight just in that.

blocks.text: So there is delight in *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, but the biggest is *davka* in the end of the deed, at the end of the seventh millennium, when it is all accomplished.

blocks.question: How come he always says that we, now, are the biggest delight, even more than the end of the seventh millennium?
blocks.text: Where is the bigger delight, now that *Chanuka* is coming: the child's graduation from *yeshiva*, or from college among the *goyim*, or the *Chanuka* play where he's dressed up like a latke? Watch the parents: the latke wins. "And that's who we are, we're dressed up like a latke."
blocks.outOfPlace: The next class (the second side of the tape) goes on with *Atika Kadisha* and its *metzach* before it rereads lines 21-23; kept here, in class order, under the passage being discussed.

blocks.text: The *metzach* is the will. The *Zohar* (*parshas Naso*): the forehead, called will, is the revelation of the whole head. It is the one part of the skull you see, facing you, the rest covered by hair. A person scratches his forehead, looks up to think; one who knows reads all kinds of things there.

blocks.question: Where does this parenthesis start, and where does it end?
blocks.text: Rereading lines 21-23, the class asks whether a parenthesis should open before *Atika Kadisha*, closing at "in detail". The parenthesis that ends "even the thought of *Adam Kadmon* does not grasp it" opens and closes on its own. The one that closes at "in detail" opens far above, at "In the language of the *Zohar*" in line 14: this whole discussion has been one long parenthesis.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 026 rereads lines 21-23 in one breath (w1248-1279, aligned to line 21); the question is about the parenthesis that closes at the end of line 23.

blocks.text: That is the whole matter: the *ratzon kadum*, still a will for Himself, includes everything. It is *Atika d'Atikin*, *Atik* of all *Atiks*, of *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, and of every sub-*Atik*, the *Keser* of each level and of each detail of a detail. Every delight and will, to the last, is this one.
blocks.outOfPlace: Said right after class 026 rereads lines 21-23 and settles the parenthesis: the summing-up of what these lines say about *Atika d'Atikin*.

blocks.question: If everything is there for a delight, where do the yucky things come from, and why do they exist?
blocks.text: Even the yucky is up there: a will has a negative, and a *chazir* (pig) comes from a negative delight and will. Isn't that just pain, no will? That's what it is: a predisposition to hate it. Whatever exists, exists because there is a delight for it, and you destroy it because in the *machshava kduma* it was hateful. Why exist? It is an Atari game: "It exists in order to blast it."
blocks.outOfPlace: Asked right after class 026 rereads lines 21-23, about their point that every detail's delight and will is included in *Atika d'Atikin*.

blocks.text: Like Amalek, the ultimate bad, which exists only for the *mitzva* to kill Amalek. Being the opposite of delight, getting rid of it is a positive delight, as two negatives make a positive. Why make it? Because destroying it is a greater delight, not because He hates it so. We hope to be rid of bad things, but the maker of the world could have made it perfect. Look at the guy's Atari game: weird creatures made to be battled and destroyed, and destroying them is a delight.
blocks.outOfPlace: Continues the question on lines 21-23 asked right after class 026 rereads them.

sections.title: Circles one beneath the other: a will that bribes the mind to find it a reason
sections.summary: In the circles each cause surrounds its effect, and the effect never reaches it. A revealed will shows how: it comes first as one undivided will, and its *chachma* and *bina* are only a will to find it a reason and to prove the reason right, as in a bribe, or in politics. All of it is the will for Himself, down to the end of the deed, which is the innermost.

phrases.he: והנה בחינת עשר ספירות דעגולים זה תחת זה הוא כידוע,
שכל עילה מקפת לעלול
ועלול לא ישיג לעילה שלו כי אם בריחוק מקום ממנו,
כאשר יהיה האופן בתוך כו'

blocks.text: So far he spoke of the *machshava kduma*; now the circles and *yosher*: each circle surrounds the one within it, and the inner does not reach the outer except at a distance of place.

phrases.he: ויובן זה מהרצון הבא בגלוי גמור
שגם שכלול הרצון הזה מי', חכמה ומדות,
phrases.en: Even though it has ten *sefiros*,

phrases.he: אבל תחלתו בא רק בהסכם א'
phrases.en: when it comes in the beginning, it just comes as one *heskem*, one *ratzon*

phrases.he: בלי התחלקות ניכר בו
והוא הנקרא עיגול רצון כללי
phrases.en: So even in a lower *ratzon*, *ratzon galui*, it first comes as an *igul klali*.

phrases.he: מקיף לכל מה שבא בתוכו מכחו דוקא,
אך בריחוק מקום

blocks.text: An analogy from the revealed will: **Even though it has ten *sefiros*, when it comes in the beginning, it just comes as one *heskem*, one *ratzon*.** So even a revealed will comes first as an *igul klali* (general circle), surrounding all within it.

phrases.he: כמו הטעם ושכל לרצון זה, שנקרא עלול שלו
אי אפשר שיהיה קרוב בערך אל עילתו, שהוא הרצון,
phrases.en: The *taam* cannot get close to the *ratzon*,

phrases.he: כי הרי אין טעם לרצון כלל כידוע,
phrases.en: because really there is no actual reason for a *ratzon*

phrases.he: ולעולם לא ישיגנו
phrases.en: it's not possible to understand it

phrases.he: אבל מכל מקום מכח הרצון נעשה עיגול החכמה גם כן
בלי התחלקות ניכר ליה כו'

blocks.text: **The *taam* cannot get close to the *ratzon*, because really there is no actual reason for a *ratzon***. It is not possible to understand it: a will has no *sechel*.
The circle of *chachma* is not *chachma* but a will of *chachma*: to find a way to get what is willed, or to rationalize the will.

phrases.he: כמו משל השוחד, שימצא טעם לרצון
phrases.en: the *shochad* is that he should find a reason for the *ratzon*

blocks.title: The bribe
blocks.text: As in the analogy of the bribe: **the *shochad* is that he should find a reason for the *ratzon***. That is called rationalization.

blocks.question: Is this like chesed and gevura of Arich dressed in Abba, where chachma is a puppet for the will?
blocks.text: This is higher: not *Abba* yet but the will itself, where it is a bribe: he wants a reason. It is not *chachma* yet; asked why he wants something, he wants to give a reason, though really there is none.

phrases.he: וגם שבטעם זה כלול גם כן מיו''ד, רצון ושכל ומדות,
אבל נעשה בבחינת כללי כו'
ועל דרך זה לא ישיגנו העיגול דבינה שנעשה מכחו,
ועל דרך זה המדות זה תחת זה עד סוף מעשה
שהוא עיגול האחרון

blocks.text: The reason includes will, intellect and *middos*, generally: a will to have a reason for the will. So the circle of *bina* is a will for an analysis of the reason.

You find this in politics: a person wants something and comes up with a reason why, and a reason why his policy has to be correct. A guy wants to be president. Why does he want it? Because of this and because of that; he feels he can help the country. "It's not really true. He really wants to be president."

sensitivity.reason: Says that a man who runs for president only wants to be president and his reasons are not true.
sensitivity.publishable: You find this in public life too: a person wants something and comes up with a reason why, and a reason why his position has to be correct. Why does he want it? Because of this and because of that. But really he simply wants it.

blocks.text: Once there is a reason for a policy, a study is set up to prove it. In *yosher* a study could prove the thing wrong; in the circles, *bina*'s whole job is to prove the *chachma* right, and *chachma*'s to prove the will makes sense.

So too the *middos*, one after the other, down to the end of the deed. You see it in politics: it could be a man you can't stand, "but he's a Republican and you're a Republican, so you like him," just because he is a Republican.

sensitivity.reason: A partisan example: liking a man one cannot stand because he is a Republican.

phrases.he: והכל ברצונו לעצמו
phrases.en: It's only the *ratzon* for Himself still

phrases.he: כלול הכל עד סוף מעשה
שהוא הפנימי מכולם כו'
phrases.en: that's the innermost of all of them

blocks.text: None of this is *sechel* or *midda*: it is all the will, **the *ratzon* for Himself still**, down to the end of the deed, where He thinks how wonderful it would be to have it happen: **that's the innermost of all of them**.

sections.title: The ratzon kadum is the daydream; doing it turns the order over into yosher
sections.summary: The *ratzon kadum* has the same ten circles, a dream of the end of the deed. When the will comes to be done, the order is reversed: the will hides in the intellect, the intellect in the *middos*, and the deed, the lowest, stands on the outside and on top.

phrases.he: וכך הוא ברצון הנעלם הנקרא רצון הקדום הנזכר לעיל,
מקור כל הרצונות
כלול מי׳ ספירות על דרך זה,
עיגול בתוך עיגול עד עיגול דסוף מעשה,
שהוא הרצון לסוף מעשה,
phrases.en: it's a *ratzon* for the *sof maaseh*

phrases.he: להיות כל אשר חפץ עושה בפועל ממש כו'
והעיגול העליון הכולל הכל הוא רצון הקדום הנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: So in the hidden will, the *ratzon kadum*: ten *sefiros*, circle within circle, down to the end of the deed, no circle of deed but **a *ratzon* for the *sof maaseh***. "The whole thing is nothing but a daydream."

phrases.he: וכשבא הרצון לעצמו הזה להיות בפועל ממש
phrases.en: when it comes to actually being *b'poel mamash*

phrases.he: הרי הוא להיפוך
phrases.en: then it has to be the opposite:

blocks.text: So **when it comes to actually being *b'poel mamash***, circles must come first: they are the daydream, the ambitions, and without them, down to the will for the deed, there is no *yosher*. *Malchus* of the circles becomes *Keser* of *yosher*.
He sits daydreaming how nice it would be, then says, "Let's actually do it," and **then it has to be the opposite**.

phrases.he: שהרצון מתעלם ומתלבש בשכל
phrases.en: the *ratzon* has to be *misalem* and *mislabesh* in the *sechel*,

phrases.he: והשכל מקיפו

blocks.title: The kid who wants a bicycle
blocks.text: Why does a man want a house? There is no reason, but the will makes up a *sechel* so he can give one. A kid wants a bicycle because he wants a bicycle; then come the reasons, riding to school and so on, which aren't really true.

In the daydream the house is infinite. To build it he must put the will aside and see what is really going on: how much money he has, whether he can afford it. The *sechel* takes over: **the *ratzon* has to be *misalem* and *mislabesh* in the *sechel***, and the intellect surrounds it.

phrases.he: והשכל מתעלם ומתלבש במדות זה תחת זה עד סוף מעשה,
phrases.en: And then the *sechel*, the *chachma*, has to be actually *misalem* and *mislabesh* in the actual, a real analysis of what's really going on here. And then it has to be *mislabesh* in the *middos*, *zu tachas zu ad sof maaseh*,

phrases.he: הוא העליון מהכל
phrases.en: That's the topmost.

phrases.he: דהיינו כח המעשה בפועל ממש
הרי בו מלובש המחשבה
phrases.en: In what a person does you can see what he's thinking,

phrases.he: ובמחשבה מלובש המדות
phrases.en: in what he's thinking you can see what his *middos* are.

phrases.he: ובמדות מלובש החכמה ובינה
ובחכמה מלובש הרצון והתענוג
ונמצא פנימי מכולם הוא הרצון והתענוג,
וחיצון שבכולם הוא המעשה
גרוע כו'
phrases.en: the lowest thing.

phrases.he: והוא בבחינת היושר כשבא בבחינת התלבשות העליון בתחתון כו'

blocks.text: **And then the *sechel*, the *chachma*, has to be actually *misalem* and *mislabesh* in the actual, a real analysis of what's really going on here.** Then in the *middos*, down to the end of the deed, which is above all.

**That's the topmost.** He made man *yashar* (straight): looking at a person you see *yosher*. You see the deed, the outside, on top; inside it are his emotions, and from what he does and says you can tell…

**In what a person does you can see what he's thinking, in what he's thinking you can see what his *middos* are**; in the *middos* are *chachma* and *bina*, in *chachma* the will and delight. The innermost is will and delight, the outermost the deed, **the lowest thing**: an actual enclothement.

sections.title: Why the ratzon kadum comes in circles and through a short line, and where speaking begins
sections.summary: The *ratzon kadum*, still within Himself, comes in circles; to reach it from the *reshimu* takes a very great contraction, a short line. In the *Ein Sof* there is no up and down, and one may not speak even of its *Malchus*; speech begins with *Adam Kadmon*. The *ratzon kadum* is His great Name, and it is not a new thing: it is part of the true *ayin*.

phrases.he: אבל בבחינת רצון הקדום הנזכר לעיל שעדיין הוא בעצמו,
phrases.en: the *ratzon kadum*: He's still inside of Himself, it didn't go to the outside yet;

phrases.he: על כן נמשך בבחינת עיגולים
phrases.en: therefore it comes in the way of *igulim*,

phrases.he: שהעליון מהכל הוא העלם הרצון הכולל הזה
ועיגול הראשון שבו הוא הרצון ותענוג לכללות כל השתלשלות שבתוכו,
ועיגול זה מקיף כללי לאבי''ע כנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: **The *ratzon kadum*: He's still inside of Himself, it didn't go to the outside yet; therefore it comes in the way of *igulim***, the highest being this all-including will, and its first circle the general *makif* of *ABYA*.

phrases.he: וראשית הקו הוא בחינת המשכה היולית
כמו קו קצר המתצמצם מעילה לעלול,
כמו מן הרצון לחכמה
phrases.en: from the *ratzon* to *chachma* there's only a little thing goes through, not the whole thing goes through

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא
כך מבחינת הרשימו הנזכר לעיל
נמשך קו בצמצום גדול מאד
דהגם שהרשימו הוא בא בהגבלה כנזכר לעיל,
אבל הוא מבחינת עולם האין סוף על כל פנים,
רק שהוא בחינת האחרונה שנעשה בקיצור כו'
מה שאין כן להיות רצון קדום שהוא בא לכלל השפעה חוץ מעולם האין סוף
רק שהוא היולי כולל הכל כו'
על כן נמשך דרך קו קצר כו'
ודי למבין

blocks.text: As **from the *ratzon* to *chachma* there's only a little thing goes through, not the whole thing goes through**, so from the *reshimu* a line is drawn in a very great contraction.

The *reshimu* is a limitation only compared to the *Ein Sof*; to what follows, it is itself *Ein Sof*. So though the *reshimu* is called nothing, coming down to the *ratzon kadum* takes a *tzimtzum* even of that: a short line.

phrases.he: (והוא מה שכתוב בעץ חיים דכל עיקר הארת הקו אינו רק להיות בחינת מעלה ומטה
phrases.en: The whole thing of the *Kav* is only to have up and down,

phrases.he: כמו ביו''ד עגולים עד סוף מעשה כו'
phrases.en: to make ten *igulim* one above the other till *sof maaseh*

phrases.he: מה שאין כן בעולם האין סוף אין שם אפילו בחינת מעלה ומטה,
רק אחדות פשוט בתכלית כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: it's all one thing

phrases.he: וגם ששיער בעצמו מה שעתיד כו'
הכל הוא בעצמותו ממש שהוא בבחינת אין סוף ממש

blocks.text: **The whole thing of the *Kav* is only to have up and down, to make ten *igulim* one above the other till *sof maaseh***: an order of wills. In the world of the *Ein Sof*, *reshimu* included, there is no up and down, between *chachma* and *bina* or *middos* and *sechel*: **it's all one thing**.

blocks.title: Knowing a man's taste
blocks.text: It is all in His Essence, not separate from it. His relation to a future deed is like taste: you can tell what a person would like, yet there is only the person, no separate will.

phrases.he: ולזה אמר בעץ חיים דגם בבחינת מלכות דאין סוף אין רשאים לדבר כו'
phrases.en: even *Malchus d'Ein Sof*, you're still not allowed to talk;

phrases.he: רק בבחינת הקו ובחינת אדם קדמון כו'
phrases.en: you're only allowed by the *bechinas hakav*

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת מקור הראשון לכל ההשתלשלות,
יוכל לבא בהשגה בריבוי ההשתלשלות עד עשר ספירות שבאצילות בבי''ע כו'
phrases.en: there you can come in *hasaga* with all kinds of *meshalim*, till you have the *mashal* of how the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus* are in *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*

phrases.he: מאחר שנקרא בשם עילת כל העילות כו' או קדמון כו'

blocks.text: **Even *Malchus d'Ein Sof*, you're still not allowed to talk**, because there is nothing to talk about: there is no separate thing to speak of.

**You're only allowed by the *bechinas hakav***, from *Adam Kadmon*; even the *Kav*'s beginning is *stima d'chol stimin*, beyond all thought. From *Adam Kadmon* **you can come in *hasaga* with all kinds of *meshalim***, down to *Atzilus* in *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, and in us. *Kadmon* here is *Adam Kadmon*, not the *Kadmon* before the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: אבל בעצמות אור אין סוף לית מחשבה תפיסא ביה, אפילו מחשבה הקדומה הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: even the *machshava kduma* cannot grasp in *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*,

phrases.he: להיות כי העולם האין סוף נבדל בערך ונקרא קדוש לגמרי מצד הצמצום הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: because the *helem* of the *Ein Sof* totally has nothing to do with after the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: ובחינת רצון קדום הנזכר לעיל נקרא שמו הגדול,
שמו גימטריא רצון,
והוא ענין יהא שמיה רבה מברך כו'

blocks.text: There, in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*, even the *machshava kduma* cannot grasp. The hidden *Ein Sof* has totally nothing to do with what is after the *tzimtzum*.
"May His great Name be blessed": that the great Name, the general will, the *machshava kduma* for the end of the seventh millennium, should come down here: *Moshiach* should come.

phrases.he: (וכידוע דבחינת אדם קדמון נקרא אדם דבריאה כו'
וכמו שיתבאר
מה שאין כן בעצמות אור אין סוף נאמר כי לא אדם הוא כו'
phrases.en: In *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* it says He's not a man.

phrases.he: וכידוע בכונות דנשמת כל חי, שהוא בחינת אדם קדמון כו'
ודי למבין):

blocks.text: **In *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* it says He's not a man.** *Adam Kadmon* already has the shape of a man; in the Essence there is no shape at all. So ends the chapter.
After the chapter: sometimes he wants commerce, sometimes not; that is the will for himself, which makes a will for a will: to be himself, he wills whatever he needs.
blocks.outOfPlace: Said after the chapter is read to the end ("And that was chapter 17"), on the ratzon kadum of the whole chapter.

blocks.text: So the *ratzon kadum* is no new creation but always there, part of the true *ayin* (nothing): not a nothing, for a nothing could not make the something, but not a something by itself. It is literally part of Him.
blocks.outOfPlace: Said after the chapter is read to the end, on the ratzon kadum of the whole chapter.

reviewQuestions.question: How does the ratzon kadum differ from the ratzon hapashut, and in what way is it still the same thing?
How can the ratzon kadum hold every detail when it is only a will for Himself? What do the bird's house and the king's suit show?
Why did the end of the deed come up first in the primordial thought?
What are Atika d'Atikin, Atika Stima'a and Atika Kadisha, and where is the will revealed?
In the circles, what are chachma and bina to the will, and why does the effect never reach its cause?
Why is the order reversed in yosher, so that the deed is the uppermost and the will the innermost?
